tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The drummer enjoys composing beats, mixing tracks, and to perform live.
The drummer enjoys composing beats, mixing tracks, and performing live.
tasks.why: The three activities use matching -ing forms.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The robotics club hopes to design a rover, to test its sensors, and entering a contest.
The robotics club hopes to design a rover, to test its sensors, and to enter a contest.
tasks.why: All three goals use infinitives.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The goalkeeper was alert, agile, and showed courage.
The goalkeeper was alert, agile, and courageous.
tasks.why: All three descriptions are adjectives.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The detective examined the lock, photographed the footprints, and was interviewing the witness.
The detective examined the lock, photographed the footprints, and interviewed the witness.
tasks.why: The coordinated actions follow the same simple-past pattern.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The recipe requires precision, patience, and being creative.
The recipe requires precision, patience, and creativity.
tasks.why: The three qualities are nouns.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The app allows users to crop photos, to adjust colors, and adding stickers.
The app allows users to crop photos, to adjust colors, and to add stickers.
tasks.why: Match to + base verb for each action.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The gymnast landed gracefully, moved confidently, and smiled with pride.
The gymnast landed gracefully, moved confidently, and smiled proudly.
tasks.why: The revised sentence consistently pairs each action with an adverb.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: Our podcast focuses on exploring mysteries, interviewing experts, and to explain discoveries.
Our podcast focuses on exploring mysteries, interviewing experts, and explaining discoveries.
tasks.why: Use three -ing phrases after focuses on.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The game rewards teamwork, accuracy, and being persistent.
The game rewards teamwork, accuracy, and persistence.
tasks.why: All three rewarded qualities are nouns.

tasks.prompt: Choose the sentence with the most consistent parallel pattern.
options: The astronaut trained to repair equipment, to navigate the capsule, and that she would handle emergencies.
The astronaut trained to repair equipment, to navigate the capsule, and to handle emergencies.
tasks.why: Use parallel infinitive phrases.

tasks.prompt: Build the sentence. Keep the listed events or items in the order shown by the sentence logic.
tasks.why: Three simple-past verb phrases describe the drone.

tasks.prompt: Build the sentence. Keep the listed events or items in the order shown by the sentence logic.
tasks.why: Three -ing phrases name the required activities.

tasks.prompt: Build the sentence. Keep the listed events or items in the order shown by the sentence logic.
tasks.why: Three infinitive phrases express hopes.

tasks.prompt: Build the sentence. Keep the listed events or items in the order shown by the sentence logic.
tasks.why: Three noun phrases name objects in the kit.

tasks.prompt: Build the sentence. Keep the listed events or items in the order shown by the sentence logic.
tasks.why: Three adjective phrases describe the game.

tasks.prompt: Choose three parallel -ing activities for a music studio.
options: recording vocals, editing tracks, and balancing sound
recording vocals, to edit tracks, and balanced sound
to record vocals, editing tracks, and balance sound
tasks.why: Match the three -ing activities.

tasks.prompt: Choose three parallel descriptions of a superhero.
options: brave, has strength, and inventive
brave, strong, and inventive
bravely, strong, and invention
tasks.why: Use three adjectives.

tasks.prompt: Complete the tournament plan: We intend ...
options: to select teams, testing equipment, and rules
selecting teams, to test equipment, and announce rules
to select teams, to test equipment, and to announce rules
tasks.why: Use three infinitive phrases.

tasks.prompt: Repair: The science fair needs organization, imagination, and to cooperate.
options: The science fair needs organization, imagination, and cooperation.
The science fair needs organized, imagination, and cooperation.
The science fair needs organizing, imagination, and to cooperate.
tasks.why: Use three nouns.

tasks.prompt: BOSS: Which mystery report contains two parallel lists?
options: The case involves a lock, a key, and searching. The detective inspected, questioned, and recovered the trophy.
The case involves a lock, a key, and a glove. The detective inspected the cabinet, questioned the captain, and recovered the trophy.
The case involves a lock, a key, and a glove. The detective inspected the cabinet, questioning the captain, and to recover the trophy.
tasks.why: The first list uses nouns; the second uses simple-past verb phrases.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Repair: The new phone is not only a camera but also stores documents.
extras.model: The new phone is not only a camera but also a document storage device.
extras.why: Balance noun phrases after not only and but also.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Write about a skateboarder using both ... and with two -ing forms.
extras.model: The skateboarder enjoys both practicing tricks and filming tutorials.
extras.why: Use matching forms on both sides of and.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Write a travel decision using either ... or and two infinitive phrases.
extras.model: We decided either to board the ferry or to rent bicycles.
extras.why: Match the grammatical forms of the two alternatives.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Write a nonparallel sentence about a concert, then repair it.
extras.model: Wrong: The concert offered dancing, singing, and to meet artists. Repair: The concert offered dancing, singing, and meeting artists.
extras.why: Explain the mismatched form and your repair.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Write a three-sentence advertisement for a futuristic museum. Include two parallel lists.
extras.model: Explore glowing exhibits, interactive walls, and virtual worlds. You can build a robot, solve a mystery, and pilot a spacecraft. Book your adventure today.
extras.why: Check that each list follows a single grammatical pattern.

tasks.prompt: The headphones stopped working the gamer switched to speakers.
options: The headphones stopped working; the gamer switched to speakers.
The headphones stopped; working the gamer switched to speakers.
The headphones stopped working; switching to speakers.
tasks.why: Each side of the correct semicolon is an independent clause.

tasks.prompt: The telescope was expensive however the astronomy club bought it.
options: The telescope was expensive, however the astronomy club bought it.
The telescope was expensive; however, the astronomy club bought it.
The telescope was expensive; however the astronomy club bought it.
tasks.why: Use ; however, between two complete clauses.

tasks.prompt: Our playlist features Sol, a jazz singer Nico, a drummer and Eva, a violinist.
options: Our playlist features Sol; a jazz singer, Nico; a drummer, and Eva; a violinist.
Our playlist features Sol, a jazz singer; Nico, a drummer; and Eva, a violinist.
Our playlist features; Sol, a jazz singer, Nico, a drummer, and Eva, a violinist.
tasks.why: Semicolons separate the whole name-and-role items.

tasks.prompt: When the power returned; the scoreboard lit up.
options: When the power returned, the scoreboard lit up.
When the power; returned the scoreboard lit up.
When the power returned; the scoreboard lit up.
tasks.why: The opening when-clause is dependent and takes a comma.

tasks.prompt: The climber reached the summit; exhausted but delighted.
options: The climber reached the summit; exhausted but delighted.
The climber reached the summit, exhausted but delighted.
The climber; reached the summit, exhausted but delighted.
tasks.why: Exhausted but delighted is not an independent clause.

tasks.prompt: The hard drive was damaged therefore the files were unavailable.
options: The hard drive was damaged; therefore, the files were unavailable.
The hard drive was damaged, therefore the files were unavailable.
The hard drive was damaged; therefore the files were unavailable.
tasks.why: Therefore links independent clauses with a semicolon before it and a comma after it.

tasks.prompt: Which sentence correctly connects two complete clauses?
options: The artist selected; blue and silver paint.
The printer jammed; the technician cleared the paper.
Unless the train arrives; we will walk.
tasks.why: Both sides of the correct semicolon can stand alone.

tasks.prompt: Which sentence correctly separates complex list items?
options: The capsule landed; the crew cheered.
The kit contains a lens, wrapped in cloth; a battery, sealed in plastic; and a cable, tied with string.
The kit contains; a lens, a battery, and a cable.
tasks.why: Each object includes an internal comma, so semicolons mark whole items.

tasks.prompt: The costume needs three accessories a mask, gloves, and boots.
options: The costume needs three accessories; a mask, gloves, and boots.
The costume needs three accessories: a mask, gloves, and boots.
The costume needs; three accessories a mask, gloves, and boots.
tasks.why: A colon introduces a list after a complete clause.

tasks.prompt: Choose the correct punctuation.
options: The trail was icy; nevertheless, the hikers continued.
The trail was icy, nevertheless the hikers continued.
The trail was icy; nevertheless the hikers continued.
tasks.why: Use ; nevertheless, between independent clauses.

tasks.prompt: Repair without changing the words: The password expired the user created a new one.
options: The password expired; the user created a new one.
The password; expired the user created a new one.
The password expired; created a new one.
tasks.why: Join the two closely related independent clauses at their boundary.

tasks.prompt: Choose the correct museum itinerary.
options: We toured the Fossil Hall, on level one; the Space Gallery, on level two; and the Robot Lab, on level three.
We toured the Fossil Hall; on level one, the Space Gallery; on level two, and the Robot Lab; on level three.
We toured; the Fossil Hall, on level one, the Space Gallery, on level two, and the Robot Lab, on level three.
tasks.why: Keep each gallery and its location together as one list item.

tasks.prompt: Since the sensor was broken; the robot missed the obstacle.
options: Since the sensor was broken, the robot missed the obstacle.
Since the sensor was broken; the robot missed the obstacle.
Since; the sensor was broken, the robot missed the obstacle.
tasks.why: Since makes the first clause dependent.

tasks.prompt: The mural was colorful moreover it covered the entire wall.
options: The mural was colorful; moreover, it covered the entire wall.
The mural was colorful, moreover it covered the entire wall.
The mural was colorful; moreover it covered the entire wall.
tasks.why: Moreover takes a preceding semicolon and a following comma when linking independent clauses.

tasks.prompt: Which semicolon is correct?
options: The cat hid; beneath the sofa.
The cat knocked over the vase; the dog ran outside.
The cat; knocked over the vase.
tasks.why: The correct semicolon connects two complete clauses.

tasks.prompt: Repair: The battery was charged however the camera would not start.
options: The battery was charged; however, the camera would not start.
The battery was charged, however the camera would not start.
The battery was charged; however the camera would not start.
tasks.why: Place ; before however and a comma after it.

tasks.prompt: Which cooking sentence joins two independent clauses?
options: The chef decorated; the cake with berries.
When the timer rang; the chef smiled.
The timer rang; the chef removed the cake.
tasks.why: Both clauses contain a subject and a finite verb.

tasks.prompt: Which technology sentence uses therefore correctly?
options: The app crashed, therefore the developer released a patch.
The app crashed; therefore, the developer released a patch.
The app crashed; therefore the developer released a patch.
tasks.why: Use ; therefore, between two independent clauses.

tasks.prompt: Choose the properly punctuated invention display.
options: The display includes SkyStep, a floating board; DreamLens, a recording mask; and EchoPen, a talking stylus.
The display includes; SkyStep, a floating board, DreamLens, a recording mask, and EchoPen, a talking stylus.
The display includes SkyStep; a floating board, DreamLens; a recording mask, and EchoPen; a talking stylus.
tasks.why: Separate whole name-description pairs with semicolons.

tasks.prompt: FINAL LOCK: Which report uses both semicolon rules correctly?
options: The alarm rang; the guard ran upstairs. Evidence included a glove, covered in dust; a necklace, hidden under a chair; and a note, written in blue ink.
The alarm rang; running upstairs. Evidence included a glove, covered in dust; a necklace, hidden under a chair; and a note, written in blue ink.
The alarm rang; the guard ran upstairs. Evidence included; a glove, a necklace, and a note.
tasks.why: The first semicolon joins independent clauses; the list semicolons separate complex items.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Repair and explain: The baker mixed; flour and sugar.
extras.model: The baker mixed flour and sugar.
extras.why: Do not separate the verb from its direct object with a semicolon.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Write a sports sentence using ; nevertheless, .
extras.model: The runner lost a shoe; nevertheless, she finished the race.
extras.why: Both sides must be independent clauses.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Give two valid repairs: The elevator stopped the passengers pressed the alarm.
extras.model: The elevator stopped; the passengers pressed the alarm. / The elevator stopped. The passengers pressed the alarm.
extras.why: A semicolon and a period are both valid boundaries here.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Create and repair a semicolon error about a video game.
extras.model: Wrong: After the dragon vanished; the gate opened. Repair: After the dragon vanished, the gate opened.
extras.why: The after-clause is dependent and cannot stand alone.

extras.prompt: EXTRA: Write three sentences reviewing a fictional theme park. Include ; however, and one complex list.
extras.model: The park looked spectacular; however, the queues were long. Attractions included MoonDrop, a rotating tower; StormRide, a water coaster; and StarPath, a glowing maze. We stayed until sunset.
extras.why: Check independent clauses, the transition comma, and whole list items.
